title: [RPG Design Guides] Thinking About RPGs as a Medium

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】媒体としてのRPGを考えてみる
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Thinking About RPGs as a Medium

blocks.source: 小説や漫画・アニメといったストーリーを持った媒体は数多く存在する。それらとＲＰＧ（正確に言えばコンピュータＲＰＧ？）に共通する部分は多くあれど、文法が異なる部分もまたある。ＲＰＧという媒体の特徴を今一度考えてみるため、その差異に焦点を当ててみたい。
blocks.translation: There are many media with stories, such as novels, manga, and anime. Although they share many elements with RPGs (or, more precisely, computer RPGs?), there are also aspects whose conventions differ. To reconsider the characteristics of RPGs as a medium, I would like to focus on those differences.

blocks.source: 基本的にはＲＰＧを中心に据えて考えるが、アクションなど他ジャンルにも当てはまる部分もあるかと思う。なお、サウンドノベル（特に選択肢を用いないもの）に付いては、性質が極めて小説そのものに近い。
blocks.translation: I will primarily consider RPGs, though some points may also apply to other genres, such as action games. Sound novels (especially those without choices), on the other hand, are extremely similar in nature to novels themselves.

blocks.source: ダンジョンの存在
blocks.translation: The Presence of Dungeons

blocks.source: ＲＰＧにおいて、かなりの時間を占めるダンジョン探索。ダンジョン内部での戦闘を含めると、総プレイ時間の大半を占めることも珍しくない。これを活用したストーリーデザインはＲＰＧならではのものといえる。
blocks.translation: Dungeon exploration takes up a considerable amount of time in RPGs. Including battles inside dungeons, it is not unusual for them to account for most of the total playtime. Story design that makes use of this can be said to be unique to RPGs.

blocks.source: 小説や漫画といった媒体においては、ダンジョンの存在は省かれることが多い。それらの媒体ではストーリーが重点に置かれることが多く、ダンジョンを長々と探索する描写を面白くすることは難しいからだろう。
blocks.translation: In media such as novels and manga, dungeons are often omitted. Those media tend to place greater emphasis on the story, and it is probably difficult to make lengthy depictions of dungeon exploration interesting.

blocks.source: ……正確にはないこともないのだが、１ダンジョンの中で何十回と戦闘を繰り返したりはしないし、ましてや１つの物語が完結するまでに数十個のダンジョンに潜るなんてこともない。
blocks.translation: ...Strictly speaking, they do exist, but characters do not fight dozens of battles in a single dungeon, much less venture into dozens of dungeons before one story reaches its conclusion.

blocks.source: ダンジョンには『長い』『ダルい』『古臭い』という面があるのも事実。ストーリー主導のＲＰＧを作りたいならば、ダンジョンを多用する以外のゲーム進行を考えてみても良いだろう。もちろん、ＲＰＧならではのダンジョン探索における面白さを追求するのも良しだ。
blocks.translation: It is also true that dungeons can be 'long,' 'tedious,' and 'old-fashioned.' If you want to make a story-driven RPG, it may be worth considering ways to progress the game without making extensive use of dungeons. Of course, you can also pursue the fun of dungeon exploration that is unique to RPGs.

blocks.source: 戦闘の扱い
blocks.translation: Handling Battles

blocks.source: 漫画等では強敵との戦いは、長々とページを費やして描写することが多い。途中、何度もピンチになったりしながら、流れの中で多くの会話を挟む。自然、敵役のキャラクターも際立つというもの。例え、一度の戦闘しかなくとも強く印象に残った悪役は数多くあげられるだろう。
blocks.translation: In manga and similar media, battles against powerful enemies are often depicted over many pages. The characters repeatedly find themselves in danger along the way, with plenty of dialogue interspersed throughout. Naturally, this also makes the villain stand out. Even villains who appear in only a single battle can leave a strong impression, and there are many examples one could name.

blocks.source: しかし、ＲＰＧではそうはいかない。なんせ、戦うのはプレイヤー自身なので、どんな流れになるかはプレイヤー次第なのだ。それでも無理矢理、漫画のような長い会話を毎ターン挟んだりするとテンポが悪くなってしまうし、どこか茶番じみてしまう懸念もある。
blocks.translation: However, things do not work that way in RPGs. After all, it is the player who fights, so the direction the battle takes depends on the player. Even if you forcibly insert long, manga-like conversations every turn, the pacing will suffer, and there is also a risk that it will feel somewhat contrived.

blocks.source: 敵役を印象付けるには漫画と比較して工夫がいることが分かる。印象付けたい敵キャラは、登場シーンや戦闘シーンといった出番を何度か作るのも１つの方法だ。
blocks.translation: It becomes clear that making a villain memorable requires more ingenuity than in manga. One method is to give an enemy you want players to remember several appearances, such as introductory scenes and battles.

blocks.source: 逆にＲＰＧ特有の表現方法として、戦闘バランスによって敵を印象付けることも可能である。「このボスは敵の大幹部だけあって、今までのボスを凌ぐ強敵だ」とか「このボスは性格通り、嫌らしい状態異常が多い」とか、能力面で感じさせてみよう。
blocks.translation: Conversely, as a method of expression unique to RPGs, it is also possible to make an enemy memorable through battle balance. Try conveying things through their abilities, such as, 'This boss is one of the enemy's top commanders, so it is a more formidable foe than any boss we've faced before,' or, 'True to this boss's personality, it inflicts a lot of nasty status ailments.'

blocks.source: 「ボスとの戦い→大ピンチ→覚醒してボスを倒す」といった少年漫画ではお馴染みの燃える展開だが、これもＲＰＧでは使いづらい。例えば、英雄伝説シリーズ等にありがちなこととして……
blocks.translation: The exciting sequence familiar from shonen manga—'battle with the boss → dire predicament → awakening and defeating the boss'—is also difficult to use in RPGs. For example, something often seen in series such as The Legend of Heroes is...

blocks.source: 戦闘画面でボスを倒す。ボスが倒れた演出。
blocks.translation: Defeat the boss on the battle screen. Show the boss collapsing.

blocks.source: イベント画面に戻ると、ボスはまだピンピンしている。そして……
blocks.translation: When the event scene resumes, the boss is still perfectly fine. And then...

blocks.source: 「中々やるな。だが、その程度で私を止められん」
blocks.translation: 'Not bad. But you can't stop me with an attack like that.'

blocks.source: とか何とか言って、切り札を出してくる。一転、ピンチに。
blocks.translation: The boss says something along those lines and brings out a trump card. Suddenly, you're in danger.

blocks.source: 誰かが助けに来てくれる or 仲間の誰かが覚醒する
blocks.translation: Someone comes to the rescue, or one of your allies awakens.

blocks.source: いかにも、それっぽい演出がやりたかったのだろうが、余りスムーズではないように思う。個人的には戦闘画面をそのまま使った方がスムーズではないだろうか？
blocks.translation: Clearly, the intention was to create a suitably dramatic presentation, but it does not seem very smooth. Personally, wouldn't it be smoother to simply continue using the battle screen?

blocks.source: 戦闘画面でボスのHPを０にする。ボスはまだ倒れない。
blocks.translation: Reduce the boss's HP to 0 on the battle screen. The boss does not fall yet.

blocks.source: 戦闘画面のまま、ボスとの会話イベント発生。
blocks.translation: While remaining on the battle screen, a conversation event with the boss occurs.

blocks.source: ボスが必殺技を放ってきて大ダメージ。
blocks.translation: The boss unleashes a special attack, dealing heavy damage.

blocks.source: ボスと因縁のあるキャラが覚醒してとどめ。
blocks.translation: A character with a personal grudge against the boss awakens and delivers the finishing blow.

blocks.source: という感じでどうだろう。ただし、編成システムによっては、因縁のあるキャラが戦闘に参加していないなんて可能性もあるのだけれど……。
blocks.translation: How about something like that? Depending on the party formation system, however, it is possible that the character with a personal grudge is not participating in the battle...

blocks.source: パーティ編成
blocks.translation: Party Formation

blocks.source: 小説や漫画では、仲間の出入りは比較的自由に行える。仲間の死亡イベントで場を盛り上げるなんて手法は古くから多用されてきた。また、仲間に別行動を取らせることによって、異なる切り口から、それぞれの見せ場を作るなんて手法もとても便利だ。
blocks.translation: In novels and manga, characters can join and leave the group relatively freely. The technique of heightening the drama with an ally's death has been used frequently for a long time. It is also very convenient to have allies act separately, creating individual moments to shine from different perspectives.

blocks.source: しかし、ＲＰＧではこういう手法は使いづらい。仲間というのは半分はプレイヤーのものであって、制作者の都合でポンポン離脱されたりしてはかなわない。「俺が考えた理想のパーティ編成を作者の都合で壊すでない！」というわけだ。
blocks.translation: However, techniques like these are difficult to use in RPGs. Allies are partly the player's characters, so it is unacceptable for them to leave one after another simply for the creator's convenience. In other words: 'Don't destroy the ideal party formation I came up with just because it suits the author's purposes!'

blocks.source: 序盤など、仲間がそろうまでは比較的、別行動を取るようなイベントも許容される傾向にある。能力紹介も兼ねて、色んなキャラクターを使わせるようにしてみよう。また、戦闘を挟まないイベントならば、別行動を取らせてもゲームシステム的な支障はない。
blocks.translation: During the early stages, before all the allies have joined, events that have characters act separately tend to be more acceptable. Try letting players use various characters while also introducing their abilities. If an event does not include a battle, having characters act separately causes no problems from a gameplay-system perspective.

blocks.source: 無口主人公
blocks.translation: The Silent Protagonist

blocks.source: ＲＰＧでしか使われない表現に無口主人公なるものがある。これは主人公のセリフをプレイヤーの想像に任せることで省略するという独特の手法だ。他の媒体ではこのような手法を取ることはまずない。強いて言えば、一人称小説で主観者の存在を極力薄くしているものが稀に見られるぐらい。
blocks.translation: One type of expression used only in RPGs is the silent protagonist. This is a unique technique in which the protagonist's lines are omitted, leaving them to the player's imagination. Other media virtually never use this technique. At most, one occasionally sees something similar in first-person novels that minimize the presence of the narrator as much as possible.

blocks.source: 文章表現
blocks.translation: Written Expression

blocks.source: 小説では心理描写などを細かく描写されることも多い。しかし、ゲームでは小説のような長々とした描写はテンポを削ぐので嫌われやすい。
blocks.translation: Novels often provide detailed descriptions of things such as characters' thoughts. In games, however, lengthy descriptions like those found in novels are generally disliked because they disrupt the pacing.

blocks.source: そもそも地の文に当たるものはないのが普通で、キャラクターの描写はセリフや視覚的な動作から行われる。人物の心理はそこから、読み取れるようにすれば十分というわけだ。
blocks.translation: To begin with, games generally have nothing equivalent to narrative prose, and characters are portrayed through dialogue and visible actions. It is enough to make the characters' thoughts discernible from those elements.

blocks.source: サブイベント（任意のイベント）
blocks.translation: Sub-Events (Optional Events)

blocks.source: ＲＰＧの特徴として、プレイヤーが任意に参加できるイベントを作れることが挙げられる。例えば、話の本流には関係が無く冗長になりそうな設定があった場合、町人や本棚を借りて情報を分散させる方法がある。
blocks.translation: One characteristic of RPGs is the ability to create events that players can choose to participate in. For example, if you have setting details that are unrelated to the main story and might make it unnecessarily long, you can distribute that information among townspeople and bookshelves.

blocks.source: 他にも、イベントの実行順序を自由にできる作品もあるが、これもＲＰＧの特性といえる。
blocks.translation: Some games also allow events to be carried out in any order, which can likewise be considered a characteristic of RPGs.

blocks.source: 選択肢・分岐
blocks.translation: Choices and Branches

blocks.source: 選択肢などによる物語の分岐という要素。ちょっと会話が変わる程度のモノから、一切合切のストーリー展開～エンディングまでが変わってしまうものもある。
blocks.translation: Another element is story branching through choices and similar mechanics. In some cases, only a few lines of dialogue change; in others, everything from the story's development to the ending changes.

blocks.source: そこまでやる作品はサウンドノベルが多く、長いＲＰＧでは普通にクリアするだけでも大変なこともあってそれほど多くない。
blocks.translation: Games that go that far are often sound novels. There are not many such RPGs, since in a long RPG it can already be difficult enough just to complete the game normally.

blocks.source: これはゲーム以外には真似できない要素。大きな分岐を伴うシナリオを長編で作るのは、制作者はもちろん、プレイヤーも大変なので、短編～中編ぐらいの方が良いかもしれない。長編でやってしまったタクティクスオウガのような例もある。
blocks.translation: This is an element that cannot be replicated outside games. Creating a long scenario with major branches is difficult not only for the creator but also for the player, so something short to medium-length may be preferable. There are also examples such as Tactics Ogre, which took on the challenge in a long-form game.

blocks.source: 盛り上がりの期間
blocks.translation: The Duration of Excitement

blocks.source: 小説のシナリオは一冊３００ページ（３～５時間が目安か？）といった長い期間で盛り上がりが最低１つあれば良い。ミステリーならば探偵と犯人との対決は大抵１回だけだろう。
blocks.translation: A novel's story can work with at least one major climax over a long span, such as 300 pages in a single volume (perhaps three to five hours?). In a mystery, the confrontation between the detective and the culprit will usually happen only once.

blocks.source: ※小説でも「短編集ならどうよ」とか「上手い作家なら途中にも、ある程度の盛り上がりを入れるよ」とかあるが、とりあえず置いておく。
blocks.translation: ※Even with novels, one might say, 'What about collections of short stories?' or 'A skilled author will include a certain amount of excitement along the way, too,' but I will set those issues aside for now.

blocks.source: 次に漫画の場合、短い期間での盛り上がりが要求される。これは市販の作品はほとんど連載物な上に、何より打ち切りの恐れもあるという大人の事情がある。「１回の放送である程度は盛り上げないと視聴率が～」というような理由でアニメも同じ。
blocks.translation: In manga, by contrast, excitement is required over short intervals. Most commercially published works are serialized, and, more than anything, there is the adult concern that they may be canceled. Anime is similar, for reasons such as, 'If each episode does not build up to something, the ratings will...'

blocks.source: ＲＰＧの場合、連載物ではないことからある程度は自由がきく。長い長いストーリー全体を通した起承転結がしっかりとした作品が評価されることが多い。
blocks.translation: In the case of RPGs, there is a certain amount of freedom because they are not serialized works. Games with a solid beginning, development, twist, and conclusion across their long, long stories are often highly regarded.

blocks.source: とはいえ、小説とは異なりクリアまで何十時間と掛かる作品で、盛り上がりが１度きりというのはどう考えても無理がある。ゲームシステムを発揮するためにも、時折ストーリー上の壁となるボスを設けて盛り上げることが望ましい。
blocks.translation: Even so, unlike a novel, a game that takes dozens of hours to complete simply cannot have only one moment of excitement. To make the most of the game system, it is advisable to heighten the drama from time to time by introducing bosses that serve as obstacles in the story.

blocks.source: 結局は、『短い間隔』『長い間隔』両方での盛り上がりが要求される。ただし、ＲＰＧではストーリー的な盛り上がりを強く狙わなくとも、ボス戦がゲームシステム側から盛り上がりを担ってくれるのは大きい。
blocks.translation: Ultimately, excitement is required at both 'short intervals' and 'long intervals.' In RPGs, however, it is a major advantage that boss battles can provide excitement through the game system even without strongly aiming for dramatic story developments.

blocks.source: ところで
blocks.translation: By the Way

blocks.source: 時々、「プロの小説家にRPGのシナリオを書かせれば良い」なんて意見を見かけるが、実際のところどうなのだろうか？
blocks.translation: I occasionally come across opinions such as, 'You should have a professional novelist write the RPG's scenario,' but what would actually happen?

blocks.source: 私見では主に課題となりそうと思うのは２点。
blocks.translation: In my view, there are mainly two points that are likely to pose challenges.

blocks.source: １．『文章表現』の観点から
blocks.translation: 1. From the Perspective of “Prose Expression”

blocks.source: 小説家は良くも悪くも長い文章を書くことに慣れすぎている。サウンドノベルならまだしも、これをそのままＲＰＧに持ってきたところで『ダルい』『冗長』といわれる危険性大。『プレイヤーに読ませる箇所』『行間を読ませる箇所』のバランスをうまく調整できるかどうか。
blocks.translation: Novelists have become too accustomed to writing long passages, for better or worse. That may be fine for a sound novel, but bringing them directly into an RPG runs a high risk of having people say they are “tedious” or “verbose.” The question is whether one can strike the right balance between “parts for the player to read” and “parts for the player to read between the lines.”

blocks.source: ２．『盛り上がりの期間』の観点から
blocks.translation: 2. From the Perspective of “Periods of Excitement”

blocks.source: さっき書いた通り、ＲＰＧでは『短い間隔』『長い間隔』両方での盛り上がりが要求される。それをうまくこなしたシナリオを書けるかどうか。
blocks.translation: As I wrote earlier, RPGs require excitement at both “short intervals” and “long intervals.” The question is whether one can write a scenario that handles both effectively.

blocks.source: この２点をクリアできるならば、いいんではないだろうか？ ファンタジー作家やＳＦ作家ならば壮大な世界設定。ミステリー作家ならば、怒涛の伏線回収とどんでん返し――というように期待できそう。
blocks.translation: If one can overcome these two challenges, perhaps it should work well. One might expect a fantasy or science-fiction writer to create an epic world setting, or a mystery writer to deliver a torrent of resolved foreshadowing and shocking twists.

blocks.source: 『盛り上がりの期間』の観点から見ると、漫画家とかも良さそうな気がする。もっとも、忙しくてそれどころじゃないって感じだろうけれど……。５年、１０年ぶっ続けで週刊連載とかマジキチ。ぼくにはとてもできない。
blocks.translation: From the perspective of “periods of excitement,” manga artists also seem like they might be a good fit. Though, of course, they are probably too busy to do anything else.... Publishing a weekly series continuously for five or ten years is absolutely insane. I could never do it.

blocks.source: ともあれ、他の媒体の長所を取り入れるも良し。あくまでＲＰＧ独自の長所にこだわるも良し。そもそも「この話、ＲＰＧには向いてないよ」と思ったならば、他のジャンル・媒体で作るのも良し。何を目指すかは制作者次第だ。
blocks.translation: In any case, it is fine to incorporate the strengths of other media. It is also fine to remain committed to the unique strengths of RPGs. And if you think, “This story isn’t suited to an RPG,” then it is fine to create it in another genre or medium. What one aims for is up to the creator.

Try conveying things through their abilities, such as, 'This boss is one of the enemy's top commanders, so it is a more formidable foe than any boss we've faced before,' or, 'True to this boss's personality, it inflicts a lot of nasty status ailments.'

texts.戦闘画面でボスを倒す。ボスが倒れた演出。: Defeat the boss on the battle screen. Show the boss collapsing.
texts.イベント画面に戻ると、ボスはまだピンピンしている。そして……: When the event scene resumes, the boss is still perfectly fine. And then...
texts.「中々やるな。だが、その程度で私を止められん」: 'Not bad. But you can't stop me with an attack like that.'
texts.とか何とか言って、切り札を出してくる。一転、ピンチに。: The boss says something along those lines and brings out a trump card. Suddenly, you're in danger.
texts.誰かが助けに来てくれる or 仲間の誰かが覚醒する: Someone comes to the rescue, or one of your allies awakens.
texts.いかにも、それっぽい演出がやりたかったのだろうが、余りスムーズではないように思う: Clearly, the intention was to create a suitably dramatic presentation, but it does not seem very smooth. Personally, wouldn't it be smoother to simply continue using the battle screen?
texts.戦闘画面でボスのHPを０にする。ボスはまだ倒れない。: Reduce the boss's HP to 0 on the battle screen. The boss does not fall yet.
texts.戦闘画面のまま、ボスとの会話イベント発生。: While remaining on the battle screen, a conversation event with the boss occurs.
texts.ボスが必殺技を放ってきて大ダメージ。: The boss unleashes a special attack, dealing heavy damage.
texts.ボスと因縁のあるキャラが覚醒してとどめ。: A character with a personal grudge against the boss awakens and delivers the finishing blow.
texts.という感じでどうだろう。ただし、編成システムによっては、因縁のあるキャラが戦闘に: How about something like that? Depending on the party formation system, however, it is possible that the character with a personal grudge is not participating in the battle...
texts.小説や漫画では、仲間の出入りは比較的自由に行える。仲間の死亡イベントで場を盛り上: In novels and manga, characters can join and leave the group relatively freely. The technique of heightening the drama with an ally's death has been used frequently for a long time. It is also very convenient to have allies act separately, creating individual moments to shine from different perspectives.
texts.しかし、ＲＰＧではこういう手法は使いづらい。仲間というのは半分はプレイヤーのもの: However, techniques like these are difficult to use in RPGs. Allies are partly the player's characters, so it is unacceptable for them to leave one after another simply for the creator's convenience. In other words: 'Don't destroy the ideal party formation I came up with just because it suits the author's purposes!'
texts.序盤など、仲間がそろうまでは比較的、別行動を取るようなイベントも許容される傾向に: During the early stages, before all the allies have joined, events that have characters act separately tend to be more acceptable. Try letting players use various characters while also introducing their abilities. If an event does not include a battle, having characters act separately causes no problems from a gameplay-system perspective.
texts.ＲＰＧでしか使われない表現に無口主人公なるものがある。これは主人公のセリフをプレ: One type of expression used only in RPGs is the silent protagonist. This is a unique technique in which the protagonist's lines are omitted, leaving them to the player's imagination. Other media virtually never use this technique. At most, one occasionally sees something similar in first-person novels that minimize the presence of the narrator as much as possible.
texts.小説では心理描写などを細かく描写されることも多い。しかし、ゲームでは小説のような: Novels often provide detailed descriptions of things such as characters' thoughts. In games, however, lengthy descriptions like those found in novels are generally disliked because they disrupt the pacing.
texts.そもそも地の文に当たるものはないのが普通で、キャラクターの描写はセリフや視覚的な: To begin with, games generally have nothing equivalent to narrative prose, and characters are portrayed through dialogue and visible actions. It is enough to make the characters' thoughts discernible from those elements.
texts.ＲＰＧの特徴として、プレイヤーが任意に参加できるイベントを作れることが挙げられる: One characteristic of RPGs is the ability to create events that players can choose to participate in. For example, if you have setting details that are unrelated to the main story and might make it unnecessarily long, you can distribute that information among townspeople and bookshelves.
texts.他にも、イベントの実行順序を自由にできる作品もあるが、これもＲＰＧの特性といえる: Some games also allow events to be carried out in any order, which can likewise be considered a characteristic of RPGs.
texts.選択肢などによる物語の分岐という要素。ちょっと会話が変わる程度のモノから、一切合: Another element is story branching through choices and similar mechanics. In some cases, only a few lines of dialogue change; in others, everything from the story's development to the ending changes.
texts.そこまでやる作品はサウンドノベルが多く、長いＲＰＧでは普通にクリアするだけでも大: Games that go that far are often sound novels. There are not many such RPGs, since in a long RPG it can already be difficult enough just to complete the game normally.
texts.これはゲーム以外には真似できない要素。大きな分岐を伴うシナリオを長編で作るのは、: This is an element that cannot be replicated outside games. Creating a long scenario with major branches is difficult not only for the creator but also for the player, so something short to medium-length may be preferable. There are also examples such as Tactics Ogre, which took on the challenge in a long-form game.
texts.小説のシナリオは一冊３００ページ（３～５時間が目安か？）といった長い期間で盛り上: A novel's story can work with at least one major climax over a long span, such as 300 pages in a single volume (perhaps three to five hours?). In a mystery, the confrontation between the detective and the culprit will usually happen only once.
texts.※小説でも「短編集ならどうよ」とか「上手い作家なら途中にも、ある程度の盛り上がり: ※Even with novels, one might say, 'What about collections of short stories?' or 'A skilled author will include a certain amount of excitement along the way, too,' but I will set those issues aside for now.
texts.次に漫画の場合、短い期間での盛り上がりが要求される。これは市販の作品はほとんど連: In manga, by contrast, excitement is required over short intervals. Most commercially published works are serialized, and, more than anything, there is the adult concern that they may be canceled. Anime is similar, for reasons such as, 'If each episode does not build up to something, the ratings will...'
texts.ＲＰＧの場合、連載物ではないことからある程度は自由がきく。長い長いストーリー全体: In the case of RPGs, there is a certain amount of freedom because they are not serialized works. Games with a solid beginning, development, twist, and conclusion across their long, long stories are often highly regarded.
texts.とはいえ、小説とは異なりクリアまで何十時間と掛かる作品で、盛り上がりが１度きりと: Even so, unlike a novel, a game that takes dozens of hours to complete simply cannot have only one moment of excitement. To make the most of the game system, it is advisable to heighten the drama from time to time by introducing bosses that serve as obstacles in the story.
texts.結局は、『短い間隔』『長い間隔』両方での盛り上がりが要求される。ただし、ＲＰＧで: Ultimately, excitement is required at both 'short intervals' and 'long intervals.' In RPGs, however, it is a major advantage that boss battles can provide excitement through the game system even without strongly aiming for dramatic story developments.
texts.時々、「プロの小説家にRPGのシナリオを書かせれば良い」なんて意見を見かけるが、: I occasionally come across opinions such as, 'You should have a professional novelist write the RPG's scenario,' but what would actually happen?
texts.私見では主に課題となりそうと思うのは２点。: In my view, there are mainly two points that are likely to pose challenges.
texts.小説家は良くも悪くも長い文章を書くことに慣れすぎている。サウンドノベルならまだし: Novelists have become too accustomed to writing long passages, for better or worse. That may be fine for a sound novel, but bringing them directly into an RPG runs a high risk of having people say they are “tedious” or “verbose.” The question is whether one can strike the right balance between “parts for the player to read” and “parts for the player to read between the lines.”
texts.２．『盛り上がりの期間』の観点から: 2. From the Perspective of “Periods of Excitement”
texts.さっき書いた通り、ＲＰＧでは『短い間隔』『長い間隔』両方での盛り上がりが要求され: As I wrote earlier, RPGs require excitement at both “short intervals” and “long intervals.” The question is whether one can write a scenario that handles both effectively.
texts.この２点をクリアできるならば、いいんではないだろうか？ ファンタジー作家やＳＦ作: If one can overcome these two challenges, perhaps it should work well. One might expect a fantasy or science-fiction writer to create an epic world setting, or a mystery writer to deliver a torrent of resolved foreshadowing and shocking twists.
texts.『盛り上がりの期間』の観点から見ると、漫画家とかも良さそうな気がする。もっとも、: From the perspective of “periods of excitement,” manga artists also seem like they might be a good fit. Though, of course, they are probably too busy to do anything else.... Publishing a weekly series continuously for five or ten years is absolutely insane. I could never do it.
texts.ともあれ、他の媒体の長所を取り入れるも良し。あくまでＲＰＧ独自の長所にこだわるも: In any case, it is fine to incorporate the strengths of other media. It is also fine to remain committed to the unique strengths of RPGs. And if you think, “This story isn’t suited to an RPG,” then it is fine to create it in another genre or medium. What one aims for is up to the creator.
